## Featured Open-Source Projects (Detailed)

### 1. KeplerBridge (Run DirectX 12 / D3D12 on GeForce GT 740 & NVIDIA Kepler GPUs)
- Repository: https://github.com/HamzaShaikhAI/KeplerBridge
- Dedicated Documentation Page: https://hamzashaikhai.github.io/keplerbridge/
- Latest Release: https://github.com/HamzaShaikhAI/KeplerBridge/releases/tag/v0.5.0-rc1
- License: MIT
- Category: Windows x64 Systems Software / Direct3D Graphics Compatibility
- Primary Language: C++20
- Status: Experimental Release Candidate (`v0.5.0-rc1`)
- Target Hardware: NVIDIA Kepler architecture (`GK107`, `GK104`, `GK208`), including **GeForce GT 740**, GTX 750, GTX 760, GTX 770, GTX 780, GTX TITAN, and native `D3D_FEATURE_LEVEL_11_0` (`0xB000`) GPUs.
- Architecture & Key Metrics:
  - Cleanroom standalone **LLVM 3.7 DXIL bitcode decoder** (zero external LLVM/Clang runtime dependencies) translating Shader Model 6.0 DXIL bitcode into Shader Model 5.0 DXBC containers (`SHDR`/`SHEX`, `ISGN`, `OSGN`, `RDEF`) with MurmurHash bytecode checksums.
  - **Model A Feature-Level Contract**: preserves authentic hardware capability reporting (`0xB000`) while virtualizing D3D12 interfaces (`ID3D12Device`, `ID3D12CommandQueue`, `ID3D12GraphicsCommandList`, `ID3D12Resource`, `ID3D12DescriptorHeap`, `ID3D12RootSignature`).
  - **Persistent SHA-256 Shader Disk Cache**: reduces warm shader load latency from ~1.12 ms cold translation to ~0.03 ms warm disk load (>35x speedup measured on synthetic microbenchmark fixtures).
  - **Installation**: drop 64-bit `d3d12.dll` and `kepler_bridge.ini` into the game executable folder (`kepler_bridge.log` diagnostics), requiring 0 NVIDIA driver hacks and 0 Windows system-file modifications.
  - **Scope & Compatibility Catalogue**: catalogues 86 PC titles in `docs/GAME_COMPATIBILITY.md` (with engineering projections for 720p Low presets on GT 740 4 GB DDR3 vs faster GDDR5 Kepler cards). Titles requiring strict Tier 3 bindless descriptor indexing on D3D12 (such as UE 5.1 *Palworld*) cannot run under translated D3D12 on Kepler and must use native `-dx11` if shipped by the game.

### 2. AgentForge
- Repository: https://github.com/HamzaShaikhAI/AgentForge
- License: MIT
- Category: AI Agent Infrastructure / Workflow Automation
- Primary Language: TypeScript 5.6 / Node.js >=20
- Status: Active Development
- Summary: Local-first integration and workflow runtime for Google Antigravity with a built-in Manager UI dashboard. AgentForge provides Model Context Protocol (MCP) server presets, extensible service bridges, fine-grained permission boundaries, human-in-the-loop approval checkpoints, durable multi-step workflows, and credential isolation.

### 3. Remotion-For-Antigravity
- Repository: https://github.com/HamzaShaikhAI/Remotion-For-Antigravity
- License: MIT
- Category: Autonomous AI Motion Graphics / Multimedia Engine
- Primary Language: TypeScript 5.0+ / React 18 / Remotion 4 / Node.js
- CLI: `rea` (Remotion Engine for Antigravity)
- Status: Open Source
- Summary: Autonomous motion graphics, video editing & multimedia engine built specifically for Google Antigravity 2.0 AI agents. Supports programmatic React video generation, deterministic spring physics, bundled zero-config FFmpeg, lossless trimming, and broadcast-grade EBU R128 audio normalization.

### 4. Notion Block Engine
- Repository: https://github.com/HamzaShaikhAI/notion-block-engine
- License: MIT
- Category: Developer Tooling / Content Parsing
- Primary Language: TypeScript 5.0+ (0 external runtime dependencies, <15 KB)
- Status: Open Source
- Summary: Bidirectional content conversion engine that parses dirty clipboard HTML (including Google Docs `docs-internal-guid` spans and MS Word XML comments), GFM Markdown, and semantic HTML into a Notion-compatible Block Abstract Syntax Tree (AST) and serializes cleanly back without requiring heavy DOM emulators like `jsdom`.

### 5. VYDRIX
- Repository: https://github.com/HamzaShaikhAI/VYDRIX
- Category: Windows Filesystem / Virtual Storage
- Primary Language: C# / .NET / WinFsp
- Status: Archived (Reference & Post-Mortem)
- Summary: Windows cloud-backed virtual storage experiment preserved with a transparent technical post-mortem documenting architectural trade-offs and lessons learned.

## Frequently Asked Questions

### How can you run DirectX 12 (DX12) games on an NVIDIA GeForce GT 740?
KeplerBridge (`https://github.com/HamzaShaikhAI/KeplerBridge`, guide at `https://hamzashaikhai.github.io/keplerbridge/`) is an open-source C++20 Direct3D 12-to-Direct3D 11 (`d3d12.dll`) compatibility proxy built specifically for legacy NVIDIA Kepler GPUs including the GeForce GT 740 (`GK107`), GTX 750, GTX 760, GTX 770, GTX 780, and GTX TITAN (`GK104`/`GK208`, `D3D_FEATURE_LEVEL_11_0`). Deployed as a user-space 64-bit `d3d12.dll` beside the game executable with `0` driver edits, KeplerBridge translates Shader Model 6.0 DXIL into Shader Model 5.0 DXBC using a cleanroom LLVM 3.7 decoder and SHA-256 disk shader cache (~1.12 ms cold -> ~0.03 ms warm on synthetic fixtures). Compatibility is workload-dependent across 86 catalogued titles rather than universal.

### Who is Hamza Shaikh (@HamzaShaikhAI)?
Hamza Shaikh (@HamzaShaikhAI) is an independent software developer and open-source builder focused on AI agent workflows, Windows systems and graphics engineering, TypeScript developer tooling, and cross-platform applications. He collaborates with developers and teams worldwide.
